name: CARRACK
full_name: Cosmic Axion Research with Rydberg Atoms in a resonant Cavity in Kyoto
summary: A historical series of cryogenic axion searches detecting individual microwave photons in a cavity with Rydberg atoms.
detection_principle: An axion signal generated in a magnetized conversion cavity couples to a field-free detection cavity, where passing Rydberg atoms absorb and read out the photons.

status.label: Multiphase project: completed experiments alongside further construction / design
status.evidence: 2001 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

collaboration.name: CARRACK Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

key_parameters.name: CARRACK I
key_parameters.value: An 8% mass interval around approximately 10 μeV

phases.name: CARRACK II
phases.description: Subsequent technology demonstrator with broader coverage.

results.summary: The 2001 report states that CARRACK I had conducted searches and II was ready; broader mass coverage was a design goal.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
